design_decisions.decision: Homegrown bash scanner over a third-party action (e.g., gitleaks-action, trufflehog-action).
design_decisions.rejected_alternative: Use `gitleaks-action` for exhaustive rule coverage + maintained pattern set.
design_decisions.rationale: User's smallest-actionable + no-bloat preference (captured in session context). The 9 high-signal patterns cover the realistic threat model for agent-authored evidence prose: well-known SaaS API key shapes, AWS / GitHub / Slack tokens, PEM private keys, bearer headers, JWTs. A third-party action would add ~50MB of binary download + license-policy review (gitleaks v8+ has org-size license terms) + an opaque rule set. The homegrown script is ~50 lines of bash, reviewable in one pass, deterministic, with zero binary dependencies. Future uplift: when an attack surface widens beyond agent-authored evidence prose (e.g., scanning the full repo on every push), revisit the action choice.

design_decisions.decision: Scope deliberately narrow to evidence/multispectrum/ + evidence/audit-chain.jsonl.
design_decisions.rejected_alternative: Scan the entire repo on every PR.
design_decisions.rationale: The FixupTask scoped to evidence/multispectrum/ specifically because facet findings strings carry agent-authored prose with the highest risk of accidental credential capture from environment / debugger / log output. Full-repo scanning would conflict with cargo-deny / dependency-pinned cargo-secrets-style checks already in the supply-chain lane and would add CI minutes without proportional risk reduction. Workflow runs in <30s on the current corpus (28 files + audit-chain.jsonl).

findings: 9 patterns + one grep invocation + one exit-code branch. No state, no config file separate from the script, no third-party dependency. The patterns array IS the policy — adding a pattern is one line.

Smoke-tested with a fabricated Anthropic-style sk-aaaa…aaaa key in a temp fixture file → scanner detects with path + line; exit 1. Adversarial coverage proves the workflow blocks merge when real secret-shape tokens appear in evidence.

Script uses `set -eu` (no `-o pipefail` because `grep ... || true` is the intended graceful-no-match path). Patterns are extended-regex via `grep -E`; portable to BSD grep (macOS) + GNU grep (CI ubuntu). Workflow timeout = 5min (generous for the corpus size).

Resolves the SOC2/FedRAMP-class evidence-corpus exposure noted in the original FixupTask (`findings strings could contain credentials`). No data-class, autonomy-ceiling, or licence surface touched. No raw secrets enter the repo via this PR (smoke-test fixture lived in /tmp and was deleted; current evidence/ tree is clean).

Audit-chain row appended with distinct timestamp_unix + session_id (OP-08). Workflow surfaces failures with path + line per match, so PR authors can locate + redact without guessing. The lane is NOT yet in branch-protection required_status_checks — same shape as F-MASTERPLAN-COMPLETION-BRANCH-PROTECTION (admin-scope `gh api PUT` deferred).

architect.rationale: Smallest-actionable kernel. The script IS the policy; the workflow IS the gate. No new subsystem, no orchestrator, no rule-engine. Patterns are the data; grep is the engine.

guardrails: Pattern set is necessarily incomplete — secret formats evolve (e.g., new SaaS providers, GCP keys, Azure AD tokens). When false-negatives are reported, add the missing pattern as a one-line patch.

Lane is advisory until added to dev branch-protection required_status_checks (admin-scope step; same shape as F-MASTERPLAN-COMPLETION-BRANCH-PROTECTION). Until then a PR author can technically bypass by merging without the check being required, though the lane will still surface red on the PR conversation page.
